title: Due Dates, Late Charges and Credit Hold on Micro Market Settlement Invoices
content:
Settlement invoices on an Unattended Micro Market Program agreement fall due the number of days after the invoice date printed against the market format, and a payment is recorded against the single invoice it settles.

## Standing of the agreement

A payment is accepted while the agreement stands active, suspended or closed, since a closed market may still carry a final settlement. The standing and the balance outstanding are read from the company's records for that agreement before the payment is taken.

## Part payments and overpayments

The clause reading "A part payment settles the named invoice in part and never spills onto another" is **no longer in force**, having been superseded by the current basis on which the amount tendered against a settlement invoice is worked out. An overpayment leaves the excess on the agreement to be applied to the next settlement raised.

## Late charges

A late charge is the monthly late percentage printed against the market format applied to the amount still outstanding once the grace days printed against the same format have passed, held to the late charge ceiling printed against that format.

Where a settlement is disputed in writing before the grace days expire, no late charge is raised while the dispute stands open, and the due date is not moved.

## Credit hold

Once a settlement invoice is past due by the credit hold threshold printed against the market format, restocking stops and the market is drawn down to empty rather than replenished, until the balance is settled.

superseded_clauses: A part payment settles the named invoice in part and never spills onto another
